Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

challenge verb and noun

to a contest

also challenge someone, call out, take on, rival, vie with

classical

Plaut. Curc. 355: prōvocat mē in āleam
Liv. 2.10.8: nunc singulōs prōvocāre

prōvocō, prōvocāre, prōvocāvī, prōvocātum

verb, first conjugation: ad or in with the accusative of the contest

challenge, call out (to a game, a race, a fight)

Lewis & Short: “to call out, challenge, invite one to any thing (as to play, sing, drink, fight)”: ad pugnam (Cic. Tusc. 4.49), to a race (Plautus). Of rivals, to compete with (Quintilian, Pliny). “A challenge” is best given with the verb: prōvocātiō is classically an appeal to the people.

Other words

  • lacessō, lacessere, lacessīvī, lacessītum — provoke, challenge

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.20: nisi lacessītus injūriā

Examples

  • postquam cēnātī atque appōtī, tālōs poscit sibi in manum, prōvocat mē in āleam, ut ego lūdam

    after dinner and drinks he calls for the dice and challenges me to a gamePlaut. Curc. 354–355

  • circumferēns inde trucēs mināciter oculōs ad procerēs Etruscōrum nunc singulōs prōvocāre, nunc increpāre omnēs

    then, turning fierce and threatening eyes on the Etruscan leaders, he challenged them one by one and taunted them allLiv. 2.10.8

  • elegīā quoque Graecōs prōvocāmus

    in elegy too we challenge the GreeksQuint. 10.1.93

See also play, win, lose.

SourcesLewis & Short: provoco · Lewis & Short: lacesso
